title: Which one fails?
examObjective: Applying correct syntax to write DataWeave transformations to coerce, format, order, and filter data
basics: A `match` without `else` compiles, but if a value reaches it that no case accepts, the script fails at run time. An evaluator that knows `+`, `-` and `*` will fail on any tree that contains another operator.
prompt: Each script evaluates a tree with the same evaluator, which handles `+`, `-` and `*` and has no `else`. **Which one fails?**

options:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun ev(e) = e match {
  case n is Number -> n
  case x if x.op == "+" -> ev(x.l) + ev(x.r)
  case x if x.op == "-" -> ev(x.l) - ev(x.r)
  case x if x.op == "*" -> ev(x.l) * ev(x.r)
}
---
ev(5)

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun ev(e) = e match {
  case n is Number -> n
  case x if x.op == "+" -> ev(x.l) + ev(x.r)
  case x if x.op == "-" -> ev(x.l) - ev(x.r)
  case x if x.op == "*" -> ev(x.l) * ev(x.r)
}
---
ev({ op: "*", l: { op: "+", l: 1, r: 2 }, r: 4 })

explanation.approach: No case accepts an operator of "/", and there is no `else`, so the match throws. A bare Number is a valid tree: it is the leaf case. A negative result is not an error.
